subject: Economy
sub_topic: Central Board of Direct Taxes — CBDT

concepts.name: CBDT: Statutory Basis and Constitutional Positioning
key_dimensions: Established under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963 — NOT the Income Tax Act, 1961 (common UPSC trap)
Relationship with Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) — administrative vs. functional control
Distinction between CBDT (direct taxes) and CBIC (indirect taxes) — parallel statutory bodies under same ministry
Whether CBDT is a constitutional body, statutory body, or executive body — classification trap

concepts.name: CBDT vs CBIC: Structural and Functional Comparison
key_dimensions: CBDT handles Income Tax, whereas CBIC handles GST, Customs, Central Excise — jurisdictional boundary
Both are statutory bodies under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963 — common origin, different mandates
Reporting structure: both under Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance — but separate cadre control
UPSC trap: CBIC was formerly called Central Board of Excise and Customs (CBEC) — renamed in 2018

concepts.name: Composition and Appointment of CBDT
key_dimensions: Headed by a Chairman with multiple members (typically 6 members) — not a single-headed body
Members are senior IRS (Income Tax cadre) officers — not open to lateral entry traditionally
Appointment by President of India on recommendation of the Finance Ministry — executive appointment
Distinction from quasi-judicial bodies: CBDT is primarily an administrative/policy body

concepts.name: CBDT's Role in Tax Policy Formulation vs. Tax Administration
key_dimensions: CBDT formulates policy for direct tax laws — advisory role to the Finance Ministry
Administrative control over Income Tax Department field formations across India
Difference between CBDT issuing Circulars (binding on tax authorities, NOT on taxpayers) and Notifications (statutory, binding on all)
UPSC trap: CBDT Circulars cannot override statutory provisions of the Income Tax Act

concepts.name: CBDT Circulars, Instructions, and Notifications: Legal Hierarchy
key_dimensions: Circulars: binding on Income Tax officers but NOT on courts or taxpayers — Supreme Court settled in UCO Bank case
Notifications: issued under specific sections of Income Tax Act — have statutory force
Instructions: internal administrative directions — least legal force
UPSC trap: a beneficial circular can be claimed by taxpayer even if not mandatory on them — judicial interpretation angle

concepts.name: CBDT and the Income Tax Act, 1961: Administrative Architecture
key_dimensions: CBDT administers the Income Tax Act, 1961 and Wealth Tax Act (now abolished) — scope clarification
Power to prescribe forms, rules, and procedures under delegated legislation
CBDT's role in framing Income Tax Rules, 1962 — subordinate legislation angle
Sunset provisions and CBDT's power to extend deadlines — pandemic-era extensions as example

concepts.name: Direct Tax Code (DTC) and CBDT's Role in Tax Reform
key_dimensions: DTC was proposed to replace Income Tax Act, 1961 — simplification objective
Multiple DTC drafts (2009, 2013) and why they were not implemented — CBDT's advisory role in revision
Task Force on Direct Tax Code (2017) — Arbind Modi Committee recommendations
Current status: New Tax Regime under Section 115BAC as partial DTC implementation — distinction from full DTC

concepts.name: Faceless Assessment Scheme and CBDT's Administrative Innovation
key_dimensions: Faceless Assessment introduced under Section 144B of Income Tax Act — CBDT's role in operationalization
Three pillars: Faceless Assessment, Faceless Appeal, Faceless Penalty — phased rollout
Objective: eliminate human interface, reduce corruption — technology-governance linkage
UPSC trap: Faceless Assessment does NOT apply to certain cases (search assessments, international tax matters) — exceptions

concepts.name: Permanent Account Number (PAN) and Aadhaar Linkage: CBDT's Regulatory Role
key_dimensions: PAN issued under Section 139A of Income Tax Act — CBDT administers PAN system
Mandatory Aadhaar-PAN linking under Section 139AA — Supreme Court upheld in Binoy Viswam case 2017
PAN as a common identifier across financial transactions — CBDT's data aggregation function
Consequences of PAN becoming inoperative — CBDT circulars on deadline extensions (2023 controversy)

concepts.name: Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) Framework: CBDT's Oversight
key_dimensions: TDS as a withholding tax mechanism — CBDT prescribes rates and thresholds via notifications
TRACES (TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System) — CBDT's digital infrastructure
Section 194 series — CBDT's power to introduce new TDS provisions (e.g., Section 194P for senior citizens)
UPSC trap: TDS rates in Finance Act vs. rates prescribed by CBDT notification — hierarchy of sources

concepts.name: CBDT and International Taxation: DTAA and Transfer Pricing
key_dimensions: CBDT administers Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) — Section 90 and 90A of IT Act
Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) — CBDT's competent authority role in bilateral/multilateral APAs
Transfer Pricing regulations under Sections 92–92F — CBDT prescribes methods and documentation norms
UPSC trap: DTAA overrides domestic law ONLY if beneficial to taxpayer — Section 90(2) principle

concepts.name: General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR): CBDT's Enforcement Role
key_dimensions: GAAR introduced from Assessment Year 2018-19 — CBDT delayed implementation multiple times (trap)
Invocation threshold: tax benefit exceeding Rs 3 crore — CBDT prescribes procedural safeguards
Distinction between GAAR and SAAR (Specific Anti-Avoidance Rules) — CBDT applies both
Approving Panel for GAAR — independent oversight mechanism to check CBDT overreach

concepts.name: Dispute Resolution Mechanisms: Vivad se Vishwas and CBDT
key_dimensions: Vivad se Vishwas Scheme 2020 — CBDT administered direct tax dispute resolution scheme
Distinction from Sabka Vishwas (CBIC scheme for indirect taxes) — common UPSC confusion
CBDT's role in Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) — CBDT appoints government representatives
Advance Ruling mechanism — CBDT's role vs. Authority for Advance Rulings (AAR) jurisdiction

concepts.name: CBDT's Data Exchange and Information Sharing Framework
key_dimensions: Annual Information Statement (AIS) and Taxpayer Information Summary (TIS) — CBDT's 360-degree profiling
Project Insight — CBDT's data mining initiative for non-filer identification
Automatic Exchange of Information (AEOI) under FATCA and CRS — CBDT as India's competent authority
UPSC trap: CBDT shares data with CBIC, SEBI, and RBI under Section 138 of IT Act — legal basis for sharing

concepts.name: Black Money and Benami Transactions: CBDT's Enforcement Role
key_dimensions: Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) Act, 2015 — CBDT administers, separate from IT Act
Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Amendment Act, 2016 — Adjudicating Authority under CBDT's operational domain
Income Declaration Scheme 2016 — CBDT-administered one-time disclosure window (post-demonetization context)
UPSC trap: Benami law adjudication is quasi-judicial — distinct from CBDT's purely administrative functions

concepts.name: Taxpayer Services and Grievance Redressal: CBDT's Citizen-Facing Role
key_dimensions: Centralized Processing Centre (CPC), Bengaluru — processes ITRs without human interface under CBDT
Taxpayer Charter 2020 — statutory backing under Section 119A of IT Act, CBDT's obligations to taxpayers
CPGRAMS and Aaykar Seva Kendras — grievance redressal infrastructure under CBDT
UPSC angle: Taxpayer Charter lists both rights AND obligations — bidirectional nature often missed

concepts.name: CBDT's Role in Union Budget: Revenue Estimation and Tax Expenditure
key_dimensions: CBDT provides direct tax revenue projections to Finance Ministry — inputs for Budget Estimates
Tax Expenditure Statement — CBDT quantifies revenue foregone due to exemptions and deductions
CBDT's recommendation on rationalizing exemptions — link to New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC) design
UPSC trap: CBDT recommends but Finance Minister decides — advisory vs. decision-making boundary

concepts.name: Corporate Tax Reforms and CBDT's Implementation Role
key_dimensions: Taxation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance 2019 — cut corporate tax from 30% to 22% (new companies: 15%), CBDT operationalized via Section 115BAA and 115BAB
Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) — CBDT administers MAT credit utilization across years
Equalisation Levy — CBDT collects digital economy tax (introduced 2016, expanded 2020) — NOT part of Income Tax Act
UPSC trap: Equalisation Levy is NOT an income tax — collected by CBDT but governed by Finance Act provisions separately

concepts.name: Search and Seizure Operations: CBDT's Coercive Powers
key_dimensions: Power of search and seizure under Section 132 of Income Tax Act — CBDT authorizes through Principal Directors
Survey operations under Section 133A — lesser intrusion than search, no seizure of books (trap)
Post-search assessment timeline — CBDT prescribes monitoring through internal instructions
UPSC trap: Search authorizations are NOT subject to prior judicial approval — executive power, different from CBI/ED

concepts.name: CBDT and Charitable Trusts/Exemptions: Regulatory Oversight
key_dimensions: Registration of charitable institutions under Sections 12A, 12AB, 80G — CBDT overhauled with Finance Act 2020 (mandatory re-registration)
FCRA compliance linkage — CBDT coordinates with MHA for foreign-funded NGO tax treatment
Anonymous donations taxed under Section 115BBC — CBDT's anti-abuse provision
UPSC trap: Religious trusts get partial exemption but purely religious bodies don't qualify under Section 11 — distinction matters
